points.place: 俄罗斯普列奥布拉任斯科耶
points.title: 贵族青年时期
points.description: 巴枯宁出生于俄罗斯一个古老的贵族家庭，接受了良好的教育。年轻时在圣彼得堡炮兵学院学习，后进入政府工作。这一时期，他开始接触黑格尔哲学，并对沙皇专制制度产生不满。1838年，他首次被捕，随后被流放至西伯利亚。1840年，他逃离俄罗斯，开始了长达数十年的流亡生活，这一经历深刻影响了他后来的政治思想和对权威的批判。
points.descriptionEn: Bakunin was born into an ancient aristocratic family in Russia and received an excellent education. He studied at the Artillery School in St. Petersburg and later worked in the government. During this period, he began to engage with Hegelian philosophy and developed dissatisfaction with the Tsarist autocracy. In 1838, he was first arrested and later exiled to Siberia. In 1840, he escaped Russia, beginning a decades-long exile that profoundly influenced his later political thought and critique of authority.

points.title: 流亡与思想形成
points.description: 巴枯宁首先前往德国，在那里结识了魏特林和马克思，开始深入研究社会主义理论。1842年，他在《德法年鉴》上发表文章，首次提出'破坏欲是创造性的第一条件'的观点。随后他前往巴黎，结识蒲鲁东，深受其无政府主义思想影响。1844年，巴枯宁被法国政府驱逐，前往瑞士和比利时。这一时期，他逐渐形成了自己的无政府主义理论，强调废除一切国家权威，主张通过革命手段建立自由联合的社会。
points.descriptionEn: Bakunin first traveled to Germany, where he met Weitling and Marx and began to study socialist theory deeply. In 1842, he published an article in 'Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher' where he first proposed that 'the urge to destroy is also a creative urge.' He then moved to Paris, met Proudhon, and was deeply influenced by his anarchist ideas. In 1844, Bakunin was expelled from France and went to Switzerland and Belgium. During this period, he gradually developed his own anarchist theory, emphasizing the abolition of all state authority and advocating for a society of free associations through revolutionary means.

points.title: 革命活动与被捕
points.description: 1848年欧洲革命爆发后，巴枯宁积极参与革命活动。他前往布拉格、德累斯顿和巴黎等地，组织起义和宣传革命思想。1849年，他在德累斯顿起义中被捕，后被引渡回沙皇俄国。1851年，沙皇尼古拉一世亲自审讯巴枯宁，并判处终身监禁。在彼得保罗要塞和施吕瑟尔堡监狱的七年监禁期间，巴枯宁遭受了极大的肉体和精神折磨，但他始终坚持自己的信念，并在狱中完成了《忏悔录》等重要著作。
points.descriptionEn: After the outbreak of the 1848 European revolutions, Bakunin actively participated in revolutionary activities. He traveled to Prague, Dresden, and Paris, organizing uprisings and propagating revolutionary ideas. In 1849, he was arrested during the Dresden uprising and later extradited back to Tsarist Russia. In 1851, Tsar Nicholas I personally interrogated Bakunin and sentenced him to lifelong imprisonment. During his seven years of imprisonment in Peter and Paul Fortress and Schlüsselburg Fortress, Bakunin endured extreme physical and mental torture, but he remained steadfast in his beliefs and completed important works like 'Confession' while in prison.

points.title: 流放与逃脱
points.description: 1857年，巴枯宁被改为流放至西伯利亚伊尔库茨克。在那里，他与当地官员的女儿结婚，并获得了相对的自由。1861年，他利用克里米亚战争的机会，从西伯利亚逃脱，经日本、美国和英国，最终于1864年抵达伦敦。这次逃脱历时三年，行程超过三万公里，成为19世纪最著名的逃亡之一。在伦敦，巴枯宁重新投身政治活动，与马克思重逢，但两人之间的理论分歧日益加深，特别是关于国家角色和无政府主义与马克思主义的根本区别。
points.descriptionEn: In 1857, Bakunin's sentence was commuted to exile in Irkutsk, Siberia. There, he married the daughter of a local official and gained relative freedom. In 1861, taking advantage of the Crimean War, he escaped from Siberia, traveling via Japan, the United States, and finally arriving in London in 1864. This escape lasted three years and covered over 30,000 kilometers, becoming one of the most famous escapes of the 19th century. In London, Bakunin resumed political activities, reunited with Marx, but their theoretical differences deepened, particularly regarding the role of the state and the fundamental differences between anarchism and Marxism.

points.title: 无政府主义运动领袖
points.description: 巴枯宁在日内瓦成为国际无政府主义运动的核心人物。1868年，他创立'国际社会主义民主同盟'，与马克思领导的国际工人协会（第一国际）展开激烈斗争。1870年，他参与组织里昂起义，试图建立无政府主义社区。1872年，他在海牙国际代表大会上被第一国际开除，随后与詹姆斯·吉约姆等人创立'反权威主义国际'。巴枯宁晚年致力于撰写《国家制度与无政府状态》等重要著作，系统阐述了他的无政府主义理论，强调废除一切形式的权威，主张通过革命和直接行动建立自由联合的社会。1876年，巴枯宁在日内瓦逝世，终年62岁。
points.descriptionEn: In Geneva, Bakunin became a central figure in the international anarchist movement. In 1868, he founded the 'Alliance of Social Democracy' and engaged in fierce struggles with the International Working Association (First International) led by Marx. In 1870, he participated in organizing the Lyon uprising, attempting to establish anarchist communities. In 1872, he was expelled from the First International at the Hague Congress, subsequently co-founding the 'Anti-Authoritarian International' with James Guillaume. In his later years, Bakunin devoted himself to writing important works like 'Statism and Anarchy,' systematically expounding his anarchist theory, emphasizing the abolition of all forms of authority and advocating for a society of free associations through revolution and direct action. Bakunin died in Geneva in 1876 at the age of 62.

appraisal.zh: 巴枯宁被视为19世纪激进政治思想的重要代表，其无政府主义理论与马克思主义并列为当时社会主义运动的两大传统，他对权威的批判和对个人自由的强调影响了后来的反权威主义与反全球化运动。另一种看法认为，他的思想过于理想化而缺乏实现路径，革命策略易导向暴力破坏，与马克思论战时被指不懂历史规律与阶级斗争，其组织大规模社会变革的能力也受到质疑。
appraisal.en: Bakunin is regarded as a major representative of nineteenth-century radical political thought, his anarchist theory forming one of the two great traditions of the socialism of his day alongside Marxism, and his critique of authority and emphasis on individual freedom influenced later anti-authoritarian and anti-globalization movements. Another view holds that his ideas were overly idealistic and lacked a path to realization, that his revolutionary strategy tended toward violent destruction, that in his polemics with Marx he was faulted for missing the laws of history and class struggle, and that his theory could not effectively organize large-scale social change.

supporter.zh: 巴枯宁被视为无政府主义运动的重要先驱和理论奠基人。他坚决反对一切形式的权威和压迫，主张通过革命手段建立自由平等的社会。他的思想影响了后来的无政府主义、工团主义和自由意志社会主义运动。巴枯宁强调直接行动和群众自决，为后来的反权威主义运动提供了理论基础。他的国际主义精神和对资本主义国家的批判，至今仍对激进左翼运动产生深远影响。
supporter.en: Bakunin is regarded as an important pioneer and theoretical founder of the anarchist movement. He firmly opposed all forms of authority and oppression, advocating for the establishment of a free and equal society through revolutionary means. His ideas influenced later anarchist, syndicalist, and libertarian socialist movements. Bakunin emphasized direct action and popular self-determination, providing a theoretical foundation for later anti-authoritarian movements. His internationalist spirit and critique of capitalist states continue to have a profound impact on radical leftist movements today.

critic.zh: 批评者认为巴枯宁的思想过于理想化和乌托邦化，缺乏实现路径。他的革命策略往往导致暴力破坏而非建设性变革。与马克思的争论中，他被批评为不理解历史发展的客观规律和阶级斗争的重要性。巴枯宁的个人生活也备受争议，包括他在流亡期间与多个女性有染，以及他在革命活动中的财务不透明。此外，他的无政府主义理论被批评为无法有效组织大规模社会变革，容易导致混乱而非真正的自由。
critic.en: Critics argue that Bakunin's ideas were overly idealistic and utopian, lacking practical implementation paths. His revolutionary strategies often led to violent destruction rather than constructive change. In his debates with Marx, he was criticized for not understanding the objective laws of historical development and the importance of class struggle. Bakunin's personal life was also controversial, including his relationships with multiple women during exile and financial opacity in his revolutionary activities. Furthermore, his anarchist theory was criticized as being unable to effectively organize large-scale social change, potentially leading to chaos rather than true freedom.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，巴枯宁被视为19世纪激进政治思想的重要代表人物，其无政府主义理论与马克思主义形成了19世纪社会主义运动的两大传统。他的思想对后来的反权威主义、反全球化运动和当代激进政治仍有重要影响。在流行文化中，巴枯宁常被描绘为革命浪漫主义的象征，代表着对自由的极端追求和对权威的彻底反抗。历史学家普遍认为，巴枯宁的思想虽有局限性，但他对权威的批判和对个人自由的强调，对现代政治思想的发展做出了不可忽视的贡献。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Bakunin is regarded as an important representative of 19th-century radical political thought, with his anarchist theory forming one of the two major traditions of 19th-century socialist movements alongside Marxism. His ideas continue to have significant influence on later anti-authoritarian, anti-globalization, and contemporary radical political movements. In popular culture, Bakunin is often depicted as a symbol of revolutionary romanticism, representing the extreme pursuit of freedom and thorough opposition to authority. Historians generally agree that while Bakunin's thought had limitations, his critique of authority and emphasis on individual freedom made an indelible contribution to the development of modern political thought.

self.zh: 破坏欲是创造性的第一条件。
self.en: The urge to destroy is also a creative urge.
